Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a well-circumscribed, slightly lobulated mass in the superior mediastinum that projects behind the trachea on the lateral view, which is characteristic of an esophageal lesion. Among the choices, an oesophageal lipoma is a benign tumor known to present as a smooth, lobulated mediastinal mass in this location without invasion, fitting the radiographic appearance better than malignant or cystic alternatives.
